findings.title: Denial-cache key omits identity type and can poison renderer checks
findings.body: The denial key is built only from namespace, raw subject UID, action, name, and parent folder, ignoring checkReq.IdentityType. Anonymous subjects and the render service both commonly use UID "0"; an anonymous denial for dashboards:read on a dashboard is therefore cached under the same key as a render-service check for that dashboard. The later render check returns Allowed:false from permDenialCache before getRendererPermissions can return its wildcard read permission, incorrectly breaking rendering for up to the 30-second denial TTL. Include the identity type (or do not denial-cache synthetic identities such as renderer) in the key.

findings.title: Denial-cache key uses ambiguous underscore concatenation
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates userUID, action, name, and parent with '_' without escaping or length-prefixing. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores, so distinct triples produce the same key: for example name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both produce "..._dashboards:read_a_b_c". A denial for one resource can consequently fast-path-deny a different resource for 30 seconds. Use an unambiguous encoding such as separated, escaped, or hashed components.

findings.title: Denials caused by the stale folder tree are cached, extending folder staleness
findings.body: On a cached-permission miss Check re-queries permissions from the DB, but checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions still resolve ancestors through buildFolderTree, which returns the short-TTL cached folder tree without refreshing it. For a dashboard whose access is inherited from an ancestor above its immediate parent, a newly created/re-parented folder can therefore still produce Allowed:false, and lines 153-155 then write that result into permDenialCache. The false denial is now pinned for another denial-cache TTL even after the folder tree refreshes, partially defeating the PR's goal for newly created folders. Do not denial-cache denials that depended on the folder tree, or refresh/bypass the folder cache on the DB fallback path.

findings.title: Every denied check for a new resource name bypasses the permission cache to the DB
findings.body: If cached permissions do not allow the requested name, Check always falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which after this PR always queries the permission store. The denial cache only helps repeats of the exact same (user, action, name, parent); a caller probing or enumerating many distinct dashboard/folder names—each a distinct denial key—forces a full permission DB query per name, with singleflight only deduplicating concurrent identical requests. This removes the previous cache protection against sequential negative-check DB load and needs a bound (for example revalidate at most once per cached permission-set generation/TTL window) rather than per-resource requery.
